blocks.content: Digital Experience Monitoring (DEM) combines uptime checks with real user performance. Start with the Synthetic Monitoring CLI, then connect your frontend.
Start with an outside-in check of your website: use the CLI, then review the results.

blocks.title: Set up Synthetic Monitoring with the CLI

blocks.content: Open **Synthetic Monitoring** to get the setup command.
Copy the CLI command on the left and run it in your project folder. Follow its prompts to review and create your check. Requires Node.js 22.6 or later.
blocks.tooltip: Run this command in your own terminal and return here after creating your check.

blocks.content: After the CLI creates your check, open **Checks** and review its target, probe locations, and results. If it is missing, finish the CLI setup first.
You learned how to create a synthetic check and where to review its results.
Connect your frontend to see performance and errors from real user sessions.
Create a frontend application. Choose your preferred setup method and follow its instructions to instrument your app.
You found your frontend setup options; deploy your instrumentation changes and visit your website to send browser data.
Your application may show no data until those events arrive.

When data arrives, learn how to read it:

- [Understand your synthetic check results](https://grafana.com/docs/grafana-cloud/observe-and-act/testing/synthetic-monitoring/analyze-results/)
- [Explore frontend sessions](https://grafana.com/docs/grafana-cloud/observe-and-act/monitor-applications/frontend-observability/visualize-data/sessions/)
- [Investigate frontend errors](https://grafana.com/docs/grafana-cloud/observe-and-act/monitor-applications/frontend-observability/visualize-data/errors/)
